summary: Follow up the accepted N.1 packet by supplying contravariant finite-extension compatibility of arithmetic localisation, including ramification multiplicities on residue terms. Import the general Dedekind sequence and boundary identifications from S.3, degree-two exact sequences from T.5, and the existing N.2 finite-support, transfer and injectivity nodes. The new mathematical argument computes flat pullback before dévissage; all declarations remain plans.

nodes.title: Ramification-weighted pullback on residue direct sums
nodes.statement: For the data above define ρ_n^{B/A}: ⊕_p K_n(k(p)) → ⊕_q K_n(k(q)) as the unique additive homomorphism sending ι_p(x) to Σ_{q|p} ι_q(e(q/p)·res_{k(q)/k(p)}x), with e(q/p)=q.ramificationIdx A. Integer multiples mean repeated addition in the abelian K-group; on K_1(k)=k× this is an e-th power. A prime of B has one contracted prime; each prime of A has finitely many primes above it. The same construction is defined for any family of additive groups and homomorphisms over finite fibres, and is the typeable part of the suggested file.
hypotheses: A → B is an injective finite map of Dedekind domains; F and L are their compatible fraction fields. B is flat over A (equivalently here, finite projective).
p and q mean nonzero prime ideals, indexed using IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum; q lies over p. Residue fields are A/p and B/q, not a new prime carrier.
n ≥ 0; K_n is the connective Quillen K-group of finitely generated projectives. On regular rings the imported K/G comparison identifies it with G_n.
proofSteps: Take finite prime fibres using Algebra.QuasiFinite.finite_primesOver (the finite algebra is quasi-finite); use the existing direct-sum and prime carriers.
For each p sum its finitely many weighted coefficient homomorphisms followed by DirectSum.of. Extend these maps uniquely by DirectSum.toAddMonoid; DirectSum.addHom_ext proves uniqueness.
The output coordinate can only come from its contracted p. This proves the support bound and makes an unrestricted product unnecessary.

For identity and towers evaluate on a coordinate; the two weights multiply and residue-field extension of scalars composes. Use Ideal.ramificationIdx_tower under flatness. The all-degree residue K functor and scalar extension are imported from their exact K.1 and K.2:plus nodes, not defined here.

nodes.title: Flat pullback computed through residue dévissage
nodes.statement: Let Tor(A) and Tor(B) be the exact abelian categories of finitely generated torsion modules. Under the standard dévissage isomorphisms D_A: ⊕_p K_n(k(p)) ≅ K_n(Tor(A)) and D_B: ⊕_q K_n(k(q)) ≅ K_n(Tor(B)), one has D_B⁻¹ ∘ K_n(B ⊗_A −) ∘ D_A = ρ_n^{B/A} for every n ≥ 0. These are identifications via inclusions of residue vector spaces into torsion categories, not a claim about K_n of the nonregular ring B/q^e.
hypotheses: A → B is an injective finite map of Dedekind domains; F and L are their compatible fraction fields. B is flat over A (equivalently here, finite projective).
p and q mean nonzero prime ideals, indexed using IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum; q lies over p. Residue fields are A/p and B/q, not a new prime carrier.
n ≥ 0; K_n is the connective Quillen K-group of finitely generated projectives. On regular rings the imported K/G comparison identifies it with G_n.
proofSteps: Restrict the exact tensor functor to finite-dimensional k(p)-vector spaces V. It sends V to V ⊗_{k(p)} B/pB, a finite-length B-module. The pullback functor is exact because B is flat; it preserves torsion because A → B is injective.
Since pB ≠ 0, use IsDedekindDomain.quotientEquivPiFactors and the ramification-index factor-count equality to decompose B/pB into the q-primary factors B/q^{e(q/p)} for q|p.

For a fixed q, filter the coefficient module B/q^e by the images of q^j for 0 ≤ j ≤ e. Reuse Ideal.quotientRangePowQuotSuccInclusionEquiv to identify each successive quotient with B/q, linearly over A/p. Its hypotheses are q nonzero prime, B Dedekind and a nonzero primed ramification index; Ideal.ramificationIdx_pos and ramificationIdx'_eq_ramificationIdx supply this and convert to e=q.ramificationIdx A. The equivalence is constructed by multiplying by an element of q^j outside q^{j+1}, so it also commutes with B and, since q kills both sides, with k(q). Thus each layer is one-dimensional over k(q). This is an existing library equivalence, not a new graded-layer definition. Localization at q and the DVR quotient-length theorem independently check that the filtration has exactly e layers.

Tensor these coefficient filtrations with V over the FIELD k(p). Every filtration functor and quotient functor on V is exact. Choosing a basis of each one-dimensional k(q)-line identifies its exact quotient functor with V ↦ k(q) ⊗_{k(p)} V followed by the residue inclusion into Tor(B). The choices change the functors by natural isomorphisms, so do not change induced K maps.

Apply K.3/additivity-for-exact-categories (V.1.8) to this admissible filtration of exact functors. The q-block contributes e copies of residue restriction on every K_n, hence e·res. Sum the finite blocks and use dévissage and direct-sum extensionality.

Do not apply V.1.8 to the functor M ↦ M/qM on arbitrary finite-length B-modules: it is not exact (V.4.2.1). Exactness here holds because the source is k(p)-vector spaces and the fixed coefficient modules are tensored over a field.

nodes.title: Contravariant compatibility of the full localisation sequence
nodes.statement: For A ⊂ B as above and all n ≥ 0, the imported Dedekind localisation sequences form a morphism with vertical arrows res_{B/A}: K_n(A) → K_n(B), res_{L/F}: K_n(F) → K_n(L), and ρ_n^{B/A} on the residue direct sums. In particular for n ≥ 1, ∂_B ∘ res_{L/F} = ρ_{n−1}^{B/A} ∘ ∂_A, and for n ≥ 0, res_{B/A} ∘ i_{A,n} = i_{B,n} ∘ ρ_n^{B/A}, where i is the map from the residue terms to the integral term. The integral-to-field square also commutes, including the terminating K_0(F) → 0 row. Each boundary takes values in a direct sum by the imported finite-support theorem.
hypotheses: A → B is an injective finite map of Dedekind domains; F and L are their compatible fraction fields. B is flat over A (equivalently here, finite projective).
p and q mean nonzero prime ideals, indexed using IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum; q lies over p. Residue fields are A/p and B/q, not a new prime carrier.
n ≥ 0; K_n is the connective Quillen K-group of finitely generated projectives. On regular rings the imported K/G comparison identifies it with G_n.
proofSteps: If A is a field, finite injective A → B with B a domain makes B a field; both torsion categories and residue sums are zero, and scalar-extension associativity proves the diagram. Otherwise import S.3/dedekind-localisation-sequence and N.2/finite-support. Before dévissage the sequence is K(Tor(A)) → G(A) → G(F); use the exact tensor functors to form the analogous diagram for B and L.

Tensoring a finitely generated module with finite B remains finitely generated; torsion is preserved; the quotient functor to fraction-field vector spaces commutes with scalar extension by the canonical tensor-associativity isomorphism. This is an exact functor of Serre pairs.

Use the functorial K.3/abelian-localization-theorem for that diagram. It yields compatible boundary maps before residue dévissage. S.3/cartan-localisation-comparison identifies the regular-ring K/G sequences and their boundaries. Naturality for flat tensor is the commuting square of the projective-to-module inclusions with B ⊗_A − (and analogously F → L); the tensor functors preserve finitely generated projectives. Thus the middle and generic arrows are the usual K-theory restrictions.
Replace the torsion arrow using ramification-weighted-devissage. This proves both residue-to-integral and field-boundary squares, not merely equality on K_0 or K_2 symbols.
No universal injectivity is inferred from this diagram. All injectivity claims remain those of the degree-specific nodes in the accepted N.1 packet and of T.5.

nodes.title: Arithmetic rank, divisor and tame-boundary comparisons
nodes.statement: In the restriction morphism, identify K_0(k(p)) and K_0(k(q)) with ℤ by rank, and K_1 of each residue field with its unit group by determinant. Then ρ_0 has q-coordinate e(q/p)x_p and ρ_1 has q-coordinate res(u_p)^{e(q/p)}. Consequently normalized additive orders satisfy v_q(res x)=e(q/p)v_p(x), and the imported degree-two boundary β satisfies β_q(res z)=res(β_p z)^{e(q/p)}. Adopt the K-book right-linear boundary convention β_p{a,b}=(-1)^{v_p(a)v_p(b)} overline(b^{v_p(a)}/a^{v_p(b)}), so β_p{π,u}=ū; it is the inverse of T.3’s left-oriented tameSymbol(a,b). In either convention the e-th-power compatibility is identical. On the K_0 integral terms this commutes with extension of divisor ideals pB=∏_{q|p}q^e and the class-map sign [A/p]=[A]−[p]. Import the arithmetic degree-two exact sequence, including injectivity, from T.5; do not derive it here.
hypotheses: A → B is an injective finite map of Dedekind domains; F and L are their compatible fraction fields. B is flat over A (equivalently here, finite projective).
p and q mean nonzero prime ideals, indexed using IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum; q lies over p. Residue fields are A/p and B/q, not a new prime carrier.
n ≥ 0; K_n is the connective Quillen K-group of finitely generated projectives. On regular rings the imported K/G comparison identifies it with G_n.

For the arithmetic tame-kernel row take A=O_{F,S}, B=O_{L,T} with finite S and T the full inverse image. This finiteness is used by the imported arithmetic K_1 vanishing theorem, not by the ramification calculation.
proofSteps: Use field rank and determinant comparisons already supplied by N.1’s classical K_0/K_1 imports and N.2/the-three-classical-rows. Scalar extension preserves vector-space dimension and maps a unit to its residue-field image; multiplying a K_1 class e times is taking the e-th power.

Apply finite-extension-restriction-compatibility to the imported S.3 unit-valuation boundary and the T.3 comparison (through the existing S.3/N.2 boundary contracts). This gives the additive valuation and tame-boundary equations without constructing any boundary again.

Check the valuation equality against pinned HeightOneSpectrum.valuation_liesOver, converting its multiplicative power equation to normalized additive order and converting the primed two-ideal index using Ideal.ramificationIdx'_eq_ramificationIdx.

On symbols write a=π^r u, b=π^s v. The target orders are er and es. Reducing b^{er}/a^{es} gives the e-th power of the source quotient; the sign agrees because e²rs−ers is even. The extra unit in the image of π cancels. This directly checks the convention and is a test of the imported naturality result.
For the class map use [A/p]=[A]−[p] from the imported S.3 row. Its pullback becomes [B]−[pB]=Σ_{q|p}e(q/p)([B]−[q]) via the coefficient filtration, so the inverse-Picard convention is respected.

Use the existing T.5 tame-kernel, S-integer and relative S-integer exact-sequence nodes as imports; all three exact statements were read in the T.3 packet. That packet remains partial with a needs-changes review, so these are mathematical contracts rather than reviewed implementation claims. The accepted transfer node goes B → A and uses residue transfers/norms without an e coefficient; this node goes A → B.

nodes.title: Finite-extension restriction for S-integers, towers and enlargements
nodes.statement: Let L/F be a finite extension of number fields, S a finite set of nonzero primes of O_F, and T={q of O_L : q∩O_F ∈ S}. Put A=O_{F,S} and B=O_{L,T} using S.integer and the existing arithmetic carriers. The full arithmetic localisation sequences admit the contravariant morphism above with residue q-coordinate e(q/p)res(x_p), indexed by p∉S and q∉T. These morphisms compose in finite towers with the full inverse-image sets and commute with enlargements S⊆S₁ (T⊆T₁ the corresponding inverse images); the residue enlargement map discards precisely the inverted-prime summands. If an upper set T₁ strictly contains the inverse image of S, factor the map through O_{L,T} → O_{L,T₁}, apply the same projection on residue terms and do not claim that O_{L,T₁} is finite over A.
hypotheses: F and L are number fields with a compatible F-algebra structure on L; their integral ring maps are the standard ones. S is finite for this stage’s arithmetic theorem.
T is exactly the inverse image of S for the finite-projective assertion; larger upper prime sets are handled only by the explicit localisation factorization.
For a tower M/L/F all upper prime sets are full inverse images of the preceding one. No Galois, unramified or tame assumption is imposed.
proofSteps: Import N.1/S-integers-in-a-finite-extension to obtain the injective finite-projective extension A → B and compatible fraction fields.

Use integerHeightOneSpectrumEquiv to index the primes by p∉S and q∉T. Localization preserves the residue fields and local rings at these primes, so their ramification indices are unchanged; valuation_integerHeightOneSpectrumEquiv checks the normalization.
Apply finite-extension-restriction-compatibility and low-degree-ramified-restriction to A → B.

For towers, evaluate the composite at r|q|p. Residue scalar extension composes and the pinned ramificationIdx_tower gives e(r/p)=e(q/p)e(r/q); uniqueness of contraction and the finite-fibre coordinate formula yield equality of the maps after reindexing.

For S⊆S₁ use the existing N.2/S-unit-and-class-group-sequence enlargement naturality. If p is inverted then all q over it are inverted; otherwise its residue coefficient and local ramification data are unchanged. The two orders of projection and weighted pullback agree coordinatewise.

For a larger upper set factor through the finite full-inverse-image ring, then project away the additional primes. This explains the permitted general ring map without falsely assigning finiteness or a transfer to it.

gaps.title: Inherited finite-coefficient input for the odd-degree isomorphism
gaps.detail: The accepted N.1 packet records missing finite-coefficient inputs for N.5/soule-mod-l-surjectivity. Current L.1/k-theory-mod-m and L.1/bott-element supply the coefficient object, its integral K-module structure and natural Bott element. L.1/mod-m-products also plans coefficient products, with modulus restrictions and its own supplier gaps, and L.1/browder-mod-l-ring plans the finite-field Bott calculation. Their statements were read; no assertion that finite-coefficient objects or products have no owner is retained here. The N.5 owner must reconcile these existing interfaces and their hypotheses, complete generic finite-coefficient localisation with product/boundary/transfer compatibility, and justify degree-one injectivity for O_{F,S} → F. This packet closes the contravariant N.2 gap without closing that separately recorded input gap. None of the five new nodes uses the odd isomorphism or this finite-coefficient argument.

sourceIssues.locator: V.6.8 proof, standalone Chapter V, printed p. 44
sourceIssues.printed: the fact that Kn (R) is finitely generated
sourceIssues.correction: For R not of finite type over ℤ or 𝔽_q the finite generation of K_n(R) is not supplied by IV.6.9; reduce to that case by writing R as the filtered union of rings of S-integers with S finite (ℤ_(p) = colim ℤ[1/N], p ∤ N) and using that K_* and the kernel SK_n commute with filtered colimits.
sourceIssues.reason: Theorem V.6.8 is stated for every Dedekind domain whose fraction field is global, but IV.6.9 in the standalone Chapter IV PDF (printed p. 59) covers integrally closed subrings of a number field finite over ℤ and smooth affine curves over a finite field. For R=ℤ_(p), K₁(R)=R× contains the independent primes different from p and is not finitely generated. Finite-S arithmetic rings require their own localisation/finite-generation argument before the filtered-colimit reduction; N.5 retains that supplier boundary. This is a proof-scope gap, not a counterexample to V.6.8.

sourceIssues.locator: V.6.8.1 remark, standalone Chapter V, printed p. 44
sourceIssues.printed: so K₁(F; Z/ℓ) → ⊕K₀(R/p; Z/ℓ) is not onto.
sourceIssues.correction: For n=1 the boundary can fail to be onto. Its cokernel is Pic(R)/ℓ, so it is onto exactly when Pic(R)/ℓ=0; finiteness of Pic(R) alone does not imply non-surjectivity.
sourceIssues.reason: In the finite-coefficient sequence, K₀(R; ℤ/ℓ)=K₀(R)/ℓ and K₀(F; ℤ/ℓ)=ℤ/ℓ. The kernel of their rank map is Pic(R)/ℓ, which is therefore the cokernel of the preceding boundary. For R=ℤ the class group is zero and the prime valuations make ℚ^×/(ℚ^×)^ℓ → ⊕_p ℤ/ℓ onto. The preceding sentence correctly says that the n=1 analogue of the general theorem fails; this finding concerns only the unconditional non-surjectivity assertion that follows it. For a finite class group, failure occurs exactly when gcd(ℓ,#Pic(R))>1, for example class number 2 with ℓ=2.

sourceIssues.locator: V.6.8.1 proof, standalone Chapter V, printed pp. 44–45
sourceIssues.correction: Multiplication by β^{i−1} is an isomorphism ⊕K₁(R/𝔭)/ℓ → ⊕K_{2i−1}(R/𝔭; ℤ/ℓ), every element of ⊕K_{2i−1}(R/𝔭; ℤ/ℓ) has the form β^{i−1}a, and ∂(x) = β^{i−1}∂(s) = β^{i−1}a.
sourceIssues.reason: β lies in K₂(R; ℤ/ℓ), so β^{i−1}a lies in K_{2i−1}(R/𝔭; ℤ/ℓ), which is the target in the diagram that follows; the integral group K_{2i−1}(𝔽_q) ≅ ℤ/(q^i − 1) is not ℤ/ℓ in general. '∂(x) = β^{i−1}∂(x)' is a slip for β^{i−1}∂(s), s being the lift. At primes 𝔭 over ℓ the identification ℤ/ℓ ≅ K₁(R/𝔭)/ℓ also fails (K₁(R/𝔭)/ℓ has order prime to the residue characteristic), though multiplication by β^{i−1} is still an isomorphism there.
